title: Token Economics Guardian: Skunkworks for Controlled Cost Regression & Experiment Governance
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Establish a lightweight, repeatable governance & experiment cadence (skunkworks) to run aggressive cost-reduction trials (batching, KV prefetch, post-training quant profiles) while preventing regression to customer-facing latency/SLOs or quality. This ticket scopes the initial phase: hypothesis framework, experiment grid, guardrails, rollout automation patterns, and the signoff flow for wider rollout.
goals: Define a hypothesis-first experiment template for econ trials (metric targets, SLO guards, backout criteria)
Build an experiment grid spanning quantization candidates, batching strategies, and KV prefetch heuristics
Deliver a minimum viable governance dashboard showing per-experiment cost delta, latency delta, and quality signals
Create automated rollout gates that prevent deployments with >5% drop in P95 latency or >1pt drop in quality score
Document signoff workflow and cost allocation tagging for finance/ops visibility
milestones: 2025-01-22: Finalize hypothesis template and metrics definition
2025-02-05: Complete experiment grid first pass and prioritize 6 trials
2025-02-20: Instrument observability signals and lightweight dashboard (Console draft)
2025-03-10: Run first two skunkworks trials (quant-8 & batch-cells) and capture results
2025-03-25: Publish governance playbook and rollout automation RFC
acceptance_criteria: Experiment template used for at least 3 independent trials
Dashboard surfaces cost delta, P50/P95 latency delta, and primary quality signal for each trial
Automated gate blocks candidate rollout if P95 latency regressions >5% or quality drop >1pt
Signoff flow documented with named approvers from Product, Eng, and SRE
Cost allocation tags attached to experiment runs and visible in billing export

decisions: Adopt hypothesis-first template (metric targets + guardrails) to reduce noisy experiments
Use dedicated isolated pools for higher-risk quant trials and hosted for batching experiments
Require a canonical prompt set (PromptSet-A) for quality regression checks across all trials
Rollout automation will be 'signal-first' (block on latency/quality thresholds) rather than manual approvals for low-risk batching changes
tradeoffs: Conservative guardrails limit potential upside from aggressive quant profiles but protect customer SLOs
Isolating trials to Dedicated pools increases experiment cost but reduces blast radius
Relying on PromptSet-A provides repeatable quality signal but may miss edge-case regressions seen in customer traffic
risks: Undetected quality regressions in narrow prompt set leading to downstream customer issues
Inaccurate cost attribution if billing tags are missing or misapplied
Slow experiment iteration if infra hooks for rollout automation are delayed
Stakeholder friction if signoff flow becomes a bottleneck for rapid wins
